observation.visible_scene: A lattice structure made of metallic spheres connected by rods (triangular/tetrahedral mesh) sits on a white tabletop, forming a curved U/V band with a blocky section at the upper left and two long horizontal rods spanning the open top. A person wearing a gray sweatshirt has both hands at the upper-right of the structure throughout the clip. The background (white surface, a wooden edge at the right) and the camera framing stay constant.
visible_changes: For roughly the first 20 frames both hands are clustered together at the top-right node, pinching/holding the junction where the long top rods meet the right vertical lattice band; the structure itself does not move.
Near frame 21 the left hand releases that top-right node and travels down and to the left, ending by frame 41 as an open palm hovering beside the left lattice block without gripping it.
The right hand stays on the right side, shifting from pinching the top node to cradling/holding the right vertical lattice band from behind, keeping it upright.
As the left hand moves away, the top of the right vertical lattice band becomes fully visible; its size and position are unchanged, only its occlusion by the hand is removed.
The overall U-shaped framework, the left block, and the long top rods remain fixed in place; no deformation, expansion, or translation of the structure is observed.
Camera appears static; reflections on the spheres and the wooden edge at the right do not indicate motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the structure was built before this segment.
Whether the top-right rod/joint is being attached, adjusted, or merely stabilized.
What the hands do after the clip ends.
uncertain_details: Exact intent of the top-right manipulation (constructing vs holding).
Whether the right band was being extended or simply revealed once the left hand left it (occlusion vs construction cannot be distinguished).
Small finger repositionings during the held interval.
